title: The Listening Walk
strapline: Stop, stand still, and hear the whole world that's been talking all along.
intent: Children tune their ears to the sounds around them, sharpening the listening that underpins language and reading.
Children discriminate between sounds — near and far, loud and quiet, made by people, animals, weather, machines.
Children build vocabulary to describe and name sounds, and to talk about what makes them.
Children develop attention and stillness, the skill of really listening rather than just hearing.
Children connect sounds to their sources, deepening curiosity about how the world works.
implementation: Take a slow walk — garden, corridor, local street — with the sole job of listening, stopping often to be still.
Model deep listening: 'shhh... what can you hear?' and give plenty of quiet time for sounds to arrive.
Name and describe the sounds together — a bird tweeting, a car humming, leaves rustling, a door banging.
Sort sounds as you go: near or far, loud or quiet, made by nature or by people.
Record some sounds to bring back and play as a 'what was that?' guessing game.
Make a sound map — a simple drawing where children mark where each sound came from.
Repeat in different places and weathers so children notice how the soundscape changes.
key_questions: What can you hear right now?
Is that sound near or far away?
What do you think is making that sound?
Which is the quietest sound you can hear?
How is it different when we listen inside and outside?

impact.text: Children listen attentively and notice sounds around them.
Children discriminate between and describe different sounds.
Children use vocabulary to name and talk about sounds.
Children connect sounds to what makes them.
Children develop stillness and sustained attention.
Children show curiosity about the sounds of the world.

enhancements: A recorder to capture sounds for a 'guess the sound' game back inside.
A sound map or clipboard to mark where sounds come from.
A sound-lotto game matching recorded sounds to pictures.
Listening walks in different weathers — rain, wind, a still frosty morning.
A quiet 'listening spot' in the garden to return to and notice changes.

playing_exploring: Children explore the soundscape with genuine curiosity.
They hunt for the quietest and strangest sounds to share.
active_learning: Children hold still and stay focused to catch faint sounds.
They return to listening spots to notice what has changed.
creating_thinking: Children work out what is making a sound from clues.
They sort and classify sounds by their own categories.
